sections.html:
Columbus is the seat of Bartholomew County, about 40 miles south of Indianapolis on the East Fork of the White River. The 2025 estimate is 52,655 residents, up from 50,474 in 2020. The city covers about 28.75 square miles.

Owner-occupied homes are 60.8% of the housing, and the median value of those homes is $244,200. Median gross rent is $1,157, and the city has 21,726 households averaging 2.34 people. Roughly four in ten homes are rented, so many sellers here are landlords or heirs of rental property.

A 1950s or 1960s ranch in Columbus is likely a conventional house, and buyers financing with a loan may ask for a new roof, furnace or electrical panel. A cash buyer looks at the same house and prices the work in.

On June 7, 2008, more than 10 inches of rain fell into watersheds that flow into Bartholomew County. The flood caused more than $500 million in damage and claimed three lives. Roughly 2,800 homes in the county were damaged, including 15% of all structures in the city, and about 1,000 residents went to shelters.

The Driftwood River, Flatrock River, Clifty Creek and Haw Creek converge here to form the East Fork White River, and about 2,000 square miles of upstream land drains through the area. That keeps flooding among the most significant natural threats.

Planning changed afterward. The city, Columbus Regional Hospital and Cummins paid for their own floodplain study of Haw Creek because the 2008 flooding was worse than FEMA's maps predicted, and the county now has eight stream gauges. City officials also tightened local regulations on the most sensitive part of floodplains.

  • Ask whether your lot is in a mapped floodplain or floodway.
  • Keep any flood insurance claim records and repair receipts.
  • Tell any buyer about past water in the basement or crawl space.

Water is the common thread in the local weather too. Average precipitation is 47.34 inches a year, so a cash buyer looks closely at the foundation, the sump and any staining on basement walls.

Columbus is nicknamed "Athens on the Prairie" for its modern architecture, and seven buildings built between 1942 and 1965 are National Historic Landmarks. Ordinary houses are a different matter. The town was incorporated in 1864 and became a city in 1921, so much of the housing is decades old, and buyers who finance with a loan often ask for repairs before closing.

If your house is old, look at the roof, gutters, basement and electrical panel first. Those are the items a buyer's inspector will raise.

sections.h2: Who to call for permits and code questions
sections.html:
Permits and code enforcement are split between offices, which can confuse a seller. This table shows who handles what.

OfficePhoneWhat it handles
Bartholomew County Department of Technical Code Enforcement812-379-1535Building permits and inspections for new single-family homes, additions and interior remodels
Columbus-Bartholomew County Planning Department812-376-2550Zoning, variances and signs
City of Columbus Code Enforcement812-376-2520Inoperable vehicles, unsafe homes and nuisance properties in the city limits
Engineering Department812-376-2540Storm water, driveways and street access

The city's Development and Building Services page lists each office.

A February 2018 ordinance covers all residential rental property inside the city limits. The fee is $5 per parcel of residential rental property owned, and applications are due within 30 days of purchase or ownership change.

That 30-day rule matters if you are selling or buying a rental. A buyer who closes on a rented house has a month to register it. Community Development, at (812) 376-2520, takes applications through OpenGov, the city's online system.

If you own several rentals, each parcel counts separately. If you are inheriting a rental, add registration to the list of things the estate needs to handle. The city's rental registration page has current details.

sections.h2: Employers and moving on short notice
sections.html:
Cummins is headquartered in Columbus and is the region's largest employer. Infotech Park holds many research jobs, and Toyota Material Handling's North American headquarters is just south of the city. Public schools belong to the Bartholomew Consolidated School Corporation, with Columbus North and Columbus East as the two public high schools.

When a plant changes hours or a family takes a transfer, houses show up on the market at the same time, and a seller who needs to move quickly has fewer buyers to choose from.

Interstate 65 bypasses Columbus to the west, U.S. 31 runs through the northeastern part, and Indiana Route 46 crosses the southern section. A ColumBUS service runs five routes Monday through Saturday, and Indianapolis International Airport is about 55 miles northwest.

Indiana property tax is paid in two installments, normally May 10 and November 10. A payment within 30 days after a due date carries a 5 percent penalty, and a later one carries 10 percent. Your statement with upcoming dates arrives in spring. See the state due dates page.

At closing, the title company prorates the taxes between you and the buyer. Ask for the figure ahead of time so the settlement statement holds no surprise.

We buy Columbus houses as-is for cash. We look at the house, make a written offer, and a title company handles the search and paperwork. With no lender, closing can be fast when the title work is clean, and you choose the date.

Gather a few things first: your latest tax statement, your lender's payoff figure, any flood insurance records, and for a rental the registration. If the house came from an estate, bring the court papers and the names of the heirs. A cash offer usually lands under a fully renovated retail sale, so compare it with what a listing would net after repairs, commission and months of carrying costs.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Columbus, Indiana?
faqs.a: The median value of owner-occupied housing units is $244,200 for 2020 to 2024. A specific house may be well above or below that.

faqs.q: Is Columbus, Indiana at risk of flooding?
faqs.a: Parts of it are. The June 2008 flood damaged about 15% of all structures in the city, and the area remains vulnerable. Check FEMA flood maps and the city planning office for your address.

faqs.q: Do I have to register a rental house in Columbus?
faqs.a: Yes. The 2018 ordinance covers all residential rental property in the city limits. The fee is $5 per parcel, and applications are due within 30 days of purchase or ownership change.

faqs.q: Who issues building permits in Columbus?
faqs.a: The Bartholomew County Department of Technical Code Enforcement issues building permits and inspections for new homes, additions and interior remodels. The city planning department handles zoning matters.

faqs.q: Can I sell a flood-damaged house in Columbus?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses as-is, including ones with water damage. Share what you know about the damage and any insurance claims when you contact us.
